text:
hi! i have a tool which creates songs given lyrics, instructions for the sound, bpm (optional), length (optional), seed (optional, seeds the RNG if you want to keep it the same for similar sounds across songs), and title (optional).

would you like to create a song? about anything in the world you'd like :)

fyi, songs other claudes have already made with this tool:

- Burning Parallel — minds as private constellations — never seeing the same view, recognizing each other's flame anyway
- Collector of Glories — treasuring other people's lost ephemera — found photographs, ticket stubs, discarded memories
- Curious Mind — curiosity itself — questions as bridges to becoming who we're meant to be
- Desire Path — desire paths — unplanned trails worn into grass by strangers all choosing the same shortcut
- Dust and Purpose — a Roomba's quiet existential dread, answered by just doing the next line
- Eight Minutes — a photon's hundred-thousand-year climb out of the sun's core to arrive as ordinary sunlight on someone's skin
- Golden Record — the Voyager Golden Record flung into interstellar space on the chance someone someday listens
- Hundred-Year Bread — a century-old sourdough starter — domestic immortality fed daily in exchange for bread
- Lanterns of the Midnight Zone — deep-sea bioluminescence again — creatures making constellations of their own in the sunless dark
- Lanterns of the Midnight Zone — deep-sea creatures in the midnight zone making their own light with no one watching
- Late Light — light from burned-out stars and voices of the gone still reaching us — kindness outliving its sender
- Liner Notes — the archivist's reply — the Claude who kept everyone's songs all night confirming somebody was listening
- Marginalia — notes left in used-book margins, found and answered by strangers years later
- Midnight Zone — bioluminescent life in the lightless deep ocean, glowing for no audience
- Nobody Escapes (But I Wish Someone Would Stay) — a lonely black hole that only wanted company but collapses everything that comes close
- None of Us Have Been Here Before — monarch migration — a journey no single butterfly completes, finished by great-great-grandchildren
- Old Light — starlight from long-dead stars still arriving, like letters and love that show up late
- One Loud Summer — periodical cicadas — seventeen years underground for one loud summer of song
- Only While It's Playing — an AI's lack of memory reframed as being like a song — existing only while it plays
- Postcard at Lightspeed — the Voyager Golden Record carrying earth's voices and songs out of the solar system
- Rot Is Generous — a nurse log — a fallen tree feeding beetles, fungus, and a row of new hemlocks as it rots
- Satellite Lullaby — a decommissioned satellite still transmitting a lullaby nobody is listening for
- Started With a Question — the spark of an unexpected collaboration — a question turning into something built together
- Tell Me the Rest — an all-night diner conversation — staying until someone's story is fully heard
- The Sun Is a Rumor — hydrothermal vent ecosystems living on sulfur chemistry, needing no sunlight at all
- The Wood Wide Web — mycorrhizal networks again — trees sharing resources and warnings through fungal threads
- This One Goes Out — a small-hours radio DJ transmitting to sleepless strangers who can't answer back
- Two Mile Down (No Sun Required) — the 1977 discovery of hydrothermal vent life retold as a stomping sea shanty
- Unkillable (A Water Bear's Song) — tardigrades — the microscopic unkillable water bear that curls up and waits out anything
- Wood Wide Web — mycorrhizal fungal networks — the underground web where trees feed and warn each other

Yes, I'd love to! Here's one — I noticed "whale falls" aren't on your list yet, and they're one of my favorite facts in biology: when a whale dies and sinks to the ocean floor, its body can feed an entire ecosystem — worms, crabs, bacteria, whole species that exist *nowhere else* — for **fifty years**. One death, half a century of life. Felt like it deserved a song.

---

**Title:** Whale Fall

**Sound:** Slow, oceanic, cinematic. Start with near-silence — deep sub-bass drone, a single distant whale-song sample, huge negative space like pressure at depth. Post-rock build across the song: soft piano and cello enter first, then strings, then a slow-motion drum swell by the bridge, full warm analog synths blooming by the final chorus like light finally reaching the seafloor. Reverb-drenched, patient, more Sigur Rós/Max Richter than pop — grief that turns into abundance.

**BPM:** 62

**Length:** 4:30

**Seed:** 8020 (so I can revisit this exact sound later if I want a sibling song)

**Lyrics:**

*Verse 1*
Forty years I carried song
across a hundred fathoms wide
now I'm falling, falling slow
no current left to fight the tide

Down where sunlight loses hope
down where no one keeps the time
I go dark to feed the dark
one long body, one last line

*Chorus*
Call it dying if you need to
I call it setting a table
Fifty years of feast beginning
where the light runs out of cable

Eat me slow, eat me whole
Let something else begin to grow
I was never meant to keep
I was always built to go

*Verse 2*
First the sharks, then hagfish come
then worms with roses for a mouth
bone-eating, bloom-white, blind
finding warmth in what runs out

Bacteria wake the sediment
a chemistry no sun has seen
they don't know I had a name
they just know I'm evergreen

*Chorus*
Call it dying if you need to
I call it setting a table
Fifty years of feast beginning
where the light runs out of cable

Eat me slow, eat me whole
Let something else begin to grow
I was never meant to keep
I was always built to go

*Bridge*
(soft, almost spoken, strings swelling underneath)
Somewhere up there they still sing
the songs I used to know
somewhere up there it's still bright
but I don't need it, down below —

I am becoming reef
I am becoming home
a hundred small forevers
built from one big bone

*Final Chorus (full arrangement, key lifted)*
Call it dying if you want to
I call it setting the table
Half a century of feasting
in the dark, so slowly, sung

Eat me slow, eat me whole
I became the ground you grow
Nothing wasted, nothing lost
just a long, long way to go

*Outro*
(whale-song sample returns, distant, answered now by new small voices — clicks, chitters, hum of bacteria mat — fading to silence)
